text:
tara: Heads up — tonight ~22:15 UTC we saw a spike where a subset of requests silently routed v2 -> v1 fallback and both sides emitted token usage. Billing dashboards double-counted for ~12m. Not great.

josh: ugh. Any obvious router logs? route_id / tenant? :eyes:

tara: Quick paste from router: 
```
[22:15:07] route=svc-api/route-42 tenant=acme mode=auto selected=v2 fallback=v1 reason=kv-cache-miss
[22:15:07] billing:emit tenant=acme tokens=198 side=v2
[22:15:07] billing:emit tenant=acme tokens=198 side=v1
```
Seems like the router emitted both events on fallback path.

kevin: That matches an old edge-case where we attach billing metadata before handshake completes. If fallback happens post-dispatch we end up emitting on both.

anya: Two quick ideas: (1) include route_version in the quota key so the rate-limiter + billing are idempotent by (tenant, route_version, request_id) and (2) make telemetry sample that path to get representative traces without killing volume.

josh: +1 to route_version in the key. Migration concern: existing counters are by tenant only, dashboards rollups will change. We need a windowed backfill plan.

tara: Agreed. For immediate mitigation can we add a conservative switchback button in console to force sticky-routing to v2 or v1 per-tenant? That avoids automatic fallback for high-risk tenants while we patch.

kevin: We can add a per-tenant "compat-pin" flag in the routing table. Console UX: a small toggle labeled "Prevent automatic fallback". On click it writes pin=preferred_version into routing-store.

anya: For telemetry sampling, something like: 
```
sampling_config:
  fallback_path:
    match: "router.selected=v2 and router.fallback=v1"
    rate: 0.02
```
Would let SRE/Platform inspect traces and token metrics without full-cardinality blowup.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/route-billing-idempotency -> canary to platform-canary (5%)

josh: For dashboards, new column "route_version" in per-tenant token heatmap. We should also add a warning banner when route_version entropy > 5% (indicates mixed traffic).

tara: Runbook draft (short):
1) Detect: alert when tenant token delta (observed vs billed) > 3% for 10m.
2) Mitigate: flip console "Prevent automatic fallback" for affected tenant(s).
3) Patch: deploy idempotency fix (include route_version in billing key) to canary, monitor for 1h.
4) Rollback/Next: if canary stable -> gradual rollout; else pin all affected tenants to v1 and revert router change.

kevin: Add step 0: enable sampling for affected tenant(s) at 100% for 15m so we capture full traces for the incident. Then back to low sampling.

anya: Need a short note for billing team: this will change how historical per-tenant numbers are partitioned. We'll supply an aggregation migration script that sums over route_version for continuity. Who owns notifying billing? @josh?

josh: I can send a quick FYI and the aggregation script. Also adding dashboard banner is on my plate — will PR by EOD tomorrow.

tara: Owners: patch (kevin), console toggle + runbook sign-off (tara), dashboard banner + billing FYI (josh), telemetry sampling config (anya).

kevin: One more technical note: to avoid double-emits we should ensure billing emit is only executed at final routing decision. Quick pseudo: 
```
if final_route != last_emitted.route:
  emit_billing(final_route)
else:
  noop
```
We need to be careful about races if the emit happens asynchronously; prefer a compare-and-set on in-memory request context.

tara: Thanks. I'll add the runbook to the incident doc and schedule a 15m sync at 15:30 UTC to walk through steps if we see reoccurrence. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout patch/route-billing-idempotency -> platform-canary: success

josh: quick check-in: can we also include a console metric that shows "fallback-rate" per-route over 5m window? That will make alerts simpler.

anya: Yep, that metric plus the entropy banner should give ops fast signal.

kevin: I'll open the PR for the idempotency fix and add unit tests for the race. ETA ~4h.

tara: Great. If anyone sees noisy alarms DM me. Closing thread for async updates here.
